title: Reader shapes - the framework-facing schema of the demand-side inputs
contract: The framework's demand and measurement readers consume three families of jurisdiction-published data: census attributes, household-travel-survey aggregates, and classified traffic counts. Each jurisdiction publishes them in its own vocabulary (ABS G-table column names, NSW HTS labels, RMS period labels). This document declares the shape the FRAMEWORK reads - the fields and vocabulary its own code depends on - and each city supplies a thin adapter at cities/<city>/extract/reader_shapes.py that maps its published shapes to this schema AT READ TIME. The framework resolves the adapter through src/city.py (city.readers()), the only module that knows where a city lives; no artefact is rewritten and raw downloads stay immutable.
adapter_location: cities/<city>/extract/reader_shapes.py, resolved by city.readers(). A city without one cannot run the readers listed under each family's consumed_by.

adapter_functions.mode_share_table(): Returns one row per (area_name, mode_category) for the base-year survey vintage at the survey's target-geography level, as a list of dicts with the columns below.
adapter_functions.mode_category_labels(): framework mode_category -> the label the city's survey (and its derived validation targets) print for it. Used to match target rows, which carry the survey's own wording.
adapter_functions.survey_vintage(): The survey-vintage label of the base year, exactly as the city's published files and validation targets spell it (e.g. a financial year).

columns.area_name: the survey area's name, matching city.json mode_share_target.filter_value for the target geography
columns.mode_category: one of the framework categories below
columns.trips: unlinked trip count for the category in this area (weighting quantity; null where the survey publishes shares only)
columns.linked_share_pct: the published LINKED main-mode share, percent (null where only trips are published)

hts_mode_share.note: The linked/unlinked distinction is load-bearing: a MATSim main-mode share is the linked concept (DECISIONS.md 12.1). walk_linked is the walk stage of a PT journey and is 0.0 by construction in a linked share.
hts_readers_still_source_shaped: src/build/build_activity_chains.py (hts_purpose.csv and hts_mode.csv with NSW labels, FINANCIAL_YEAR selection)

adapter_functions.total_volume_counts(): Returns the total-vehicle-volume count observations - the rows whose classification means ALL vehicles (however the agency spells that) - as a pandas DataFrame with exactly the columns below, one row per published observation (no adapter-side aggregation).

columns.period: one of: weekday, weekend - normalised from the agency's period vocabulary
columns.volume: mean daily traffic count for the period

classified_counts.note: Only the fields the framework reads are declared. Heavy-vehicle classes are consumed by city-owned measurement (the freight profile adapter), not by the framework.

consumed_by: src/build/build_population.py (residence marginals, region fallbacks, tertiary shares, published bandings and vocabularies)
src/build/build_zone_attractions.py (residence counts, workplace jobs by industry)

adapter_functions.labour_force_bands(): [(band, lo, hi)] - the age bands labour-force status is published in; the band names key labour_force cells and the population report.
adapter_functions.education_groups(): [(group, lo, hi)] - the age groups education attendance is published in, the last one open-ended.
adapter_functions.occupation_labels(): the occupation vocabulary (1-digit classification) as the city publishes it; carried into B1 as labels.
adapter_functions.income_band_labels(): the personal weekly income band labels as the city publishes them; carried into B1 as labels, whose interval the plans builder reads off the label.
adapter_functions.dwelling_types(): the framework's dwelling-structure vocabulary in the order the dwellings counts are returned.
adapter_functions.residence_marginals(zone): the per-zone counts below, or None where the zone is absent from any residence table.
adapter_functions.region_labour_force_totals(): {(sex, band): (employed, in_labour_force, not_in_labour_force, full_time, part_time, unemployed)} summed over the core zones - the fallback for empty cells.
adapter_functions.region_education_totals(): {group: (attendees, persons)} summed over the core zones.
adapter_functions.tertiary_full_time_shares(): (zone -> {band: full-time share of tertiary attendees}, {band: share over every zone}), bands 18_24 and 25_ov.
adapter_functions.residence_counts(): DataFrame [zone_id, population, dwellings_total, dwellings_occupied] per residence zone.
adapter_functions.workplace_jobs(): (jobs DataFrame [workplace_zone, jobs], industry DataFrame indexed by workplace_zone with one column per published industry division, column count).
adapter_functions.work_attendance_counts(): {total, worked_home, did_not_go}: employed persons on census day.

residence_marginals_shape.age_single_year: [(age, males, females)] for every single year the table publishes (None where unpublished)
residence_marginals_shape.age_grouped: [(lo, hi, males, females)] for the grouped ages above the single years
residence_marginals_shape.age_over: (lo, males, females) for the open top group
residence_marginals_shape.labour_force: {(sex 'M'|'F', band): (employed, in_labour_force, not_in_labour_force, full_time, part_time, unemployed)}
residence_marginals_shape.occupation: counts in occupation_labels() order, all ages 15+ and both sexes summed
residence_marginals_shape.income: counts in income_band_labels() order, all ages 15+ and both sexes summed

census_attributes.note: Adapted 3 Sep 2026 (DECISIONS.md 9.140). The framework forms every rate itself from these counts, so the synthetic population is byte-identical to the one built when the synthesiser read the ABS columns directly (verified on the 9.131 population). A second city's adapter returns the same shapes from its own census; the occupation and income labels it returns become that city's B1 vocabulary.
